name: PowerShell
desc: Adversaries may use PowerShell to perform actions like command execution and script running, often with encoded or obfuscated command lines to evade detection.

name: Scheduled Task
desc: Adversaries may abuse the Windows Task Scheduler to perform task scheduling for initial or persistent execution of malicious code.

name: LSASS Memory
desc: Adversaries may attempt to access credentials by dumping LSASS process memory to harvest cached credentials for lateral movement.

name: Clear Windows Event Logs
desc: Adversaries may clear Windows Event Logs to hide the activity of an intrusion, removing evidence of their operations.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
desc: Adversaries may obfuscate content such as scripts, executables, or commands to make detection and analysis more difficult for defenders.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
desc: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems, such as in a ransomware attack, to interrupt availability and extort victims.

name: Spearphishing Attachment
desc: Adversaries may send spearphishing emails with a malicious attachment to gain initial access to a target's systems.

name: Valid Accounts
desc: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing valid accounts to gain initial access, persistence, or escalate privileges while evading detection.

name: Remote Desktop Protocol
desc: Adversaries may use RDP with valid credentials to move laterally between systems in a network.

name: Process Injection
desc: Adversaries may inject malicious code into the address space of a separate live process to evade process-based defenses.

name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
desc: Adversaries may add programs to registry run keys or the startup folder to establish persistence across reboots.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
desc: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment to carry out follow-on actions.

name: Brute Force
desc: Adversaries may use brute-force techniques to guess account credentials when password policies allow weak or reused passwords.

name: Account Manipulation
desc: Adversaries may manipulate accounts, such as adding permissions or credentials, to maintain persistent access to a target environment.

name: Disable or Modify Tools
desc: Adversaries may disable or modify security tools, such as antivirus or logging agents, to avoid detection of their activities.
